text:
alex: Quick q — can we treat per-route API keys as strictly non-transferable (route-scoped) and require delegation tokens for any handoff? Looking at webhook ingest + async workers it feels safer, but curious about ops/UX cost.
priya: Prefer narrow keys for audit + least-privilege. Rotation + number of keys will balloon though. :grimacing:
marco: We already have connectors that hand off work to background queues. If route keys are non-transferable, connectors need to mint short-lived delegation tokens or call a broker. That adds latency and extra components.
jen: From RBAC side: route-scoped keys simplify policy enforcement (map key -> route permissions). But mapping to principals for billing/alerts gets hairy if we mint ephemeral creds often.
alex: Good point. Also concerned re: replay/reroute — webhooks sometimes degenerate to retries handled by different workers. Need some persistence of intent.
marco: Proposal: keep two-tier model: 1) route-bound "ingress" API keys (longer lived, single-use scope: ingest only) 2) operator/delegation tokens for workers (short-lived, minted by auth broker with audience claim). Workers present delegation + original route id for lineage.
priya: Sounds reasonable. What about telemetry? We need both route_id and consumer_id in logs to stitch.
jen: Agreed. Add explicit claims: {route, consumer, origin_key_id}. That way RBAC and billing can reconcile.
sre-bot: Reminder: any change touching key formats requires migration window and rollout checklist (see #release-war-room).
alex: Minimal API shape sketch: 
```
POST /auth/mint-delegation
body: {"route_id":"r_payments", "orig_key":"k_123"}
resp: {"token":"ey..", "expires_in":60}
```
workers attach Authorization: Bearer ey.. and X-Orig-Key: k_123 for trace.
priya: Need to harden the mint endpoint with rate limits + quota checks (don't want abuse to flood mint ops).
marco: Also consider fallback: if broker down, allow a degraded path where project-scoped key can be used for worker processing but with flagged telemetry and alerting. Graceful degradation > outage.
jen: That degraded path increases blast radius but acceptable if monitored and gated. Add automatic rolling disable if abuse detected.
alex: OK next steps: 1) prototype mint endpoint + DB for ephemeral tokens (TTL index) 2) small perf test for latency impact 3) docs + rollout plan with migration window and telemetry specs.
priya: I can draft the telemetry schema.
marco: I'll spike the broker prototype.
jen: I'll write the RBAC mapping matrix and the gated fallback policy.
alex: Great. Meeting to sync Wed 10am. :thumbsup:
